units.title: Unit 47 — Air travel
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 47. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Identify airport information and departure procedures, including check-in, security-related controls and boarding.
Use common terms for luggage, flight numbers, travel documents and aircraft safety.
Explain the difference between take-off and take off, and between flight and fly.
Describe arrival procedures, including landing, baggage reclaim and customs.
Use natural travel collocations to report delays and experiences on flights.

items.example: Our departure is scheduled for early Saturday morning.
items.note: The act or time of leaving at the start of a journey.

items.example: Check the departures board to find your gate.
items.note: An airport display showing flights that are leaving.

items.example: Our departure time has changed to nine thirty.
items.note: The scheduled time when a flight leaves.

items.example: The flight from London to Rome took two hours.
items.note: The journey made by an aircraft; the noun is flight, not fly.

items.example: Please write your flight number on the form.
items.note: Use flight number, never fly number.

items.example: Every passenger must have a boarding card.
items.note: Someone who travels in a vehicle without driving or operating it.

items.example: Our final destination is Lisbon.
items.note: The place to which someone is travelling.

items.pt: balcão de check-in; balcão de despacho
items.example: The check-in desk for this flight is near the entrance.
items.note: The place where airline staff check tickets and accept checked luggage.

items.example: We checked in two hours before the flight.
items.note: At an airport, confirm your arrival and complete formalities before travelling; verb is two words.

items.example: The airline checked my ticket at the desk.
items.note: A document or electronic record proving your right to travel.

items.example: The assistant will weigh your suitcase.
items.note: To measure how heavy something is; pronounced like way.

items.example: We have too much luggage for a short trip.
items.note: An uncountable noun for bags and cases used when travelling; not luggages.

items.example: My suitcase is too heavy to lift.
items.note: A large bag with a handle for clothes and other travel items.

items.example: We put our bags on a trolley.
items.note: At an airport, a wheeled cart for moving luggage.

items.pt: excesso de bagagem; bagagem acima do limite
items.example: We had to pay for excess baggage at check-in.
items.note: Luggage that exceeds an airline's permitted weight or quantity; an extra charge may apply.

items.example: Keep your passport in your hand luggage.
items.note: Bags you take into the cabin; uncountable in British English.

items.example: The aircraft is waiting near the terminal.
items.note: A plane or other vehicle that flies; the plural form is also aircraft.

items.example: Our plane is ready for boarding.
items.note: A common informal word for an aeroplane.

items.example: Show your boarding card before entering the plane.
items.note: A document, printed or digital, giving permission to board a flight.

items.example: We waited in a queue at passport control.
items.note: The place where officers check passports when entering or leaving a country.

items.example: An officer checked my passport before I left.
items.note: Check means examine carefully, not check in.

items.pt: sala de embarque; área de espera para partidas
items.example: We bought a drink in the departure lounge.
items.note: The area where travellers wait after passing airport checks.

items.pt: loja duty-free; loja livre de impostos
items.example: She bought perfume at the duty-free shop.
items.note: A shop, often at an airport, selling certain goods without some local taxes.

items.example: The take-off was smooth despite the wind.
items.note: Noun: the moment when an aircraft leaves the ground; compare the verb take off.

items.example: The plane took off just after sunrise.
items.note: Verb: leave the ground; past tense took off. Compare the noun take-off.

items.example: The flight is boarding at Gate Twelve.
items.note: At an airport, the place where passengers enter the aircraft.

items.example: We boarded the plane twenty minutes late.
items.note: Board is a verb meaning get on a plane or other transport.

items.example: Put your smaller bag in the overhead locker.
items.note: Storage space above passenger seats in the aircraft cabin.

items.example: Keep your seat belt on during the flight.
items.note: A safety strap worn while sitting in a vehicle or aircraft.

items.pt: afivelar; prender o cinto de segurança
items.example: Please fasten your seat belt before take-off.
items.note: Fasten means secure or attach firmly.

items.example: There was a delay because of thick fog.
items.note: A wait that makes something happen later than expected.

items.example: The plane moved slowly towards the runway.
items.note: The long prepared strip of land used for aircraft take-offs and landings.

items.example: Our arrival in Madrid was later than planned.
items.note: The act or time of reaching a destination; compare departure.

items.example: The aircraft landed safely in the afternoon.
items.note: When an aircraft lands, it comes down onto the ground.

items.example: The landing was difficult because of strong winds.
items.note: The noun for the act of a plane returning to the ground.

items.example: We heard an announcement about our arrival gate.
items.note: Spoken information given to a group of people.

items.pt: tripulação de cabine; comissários de bordo
items.example: The cabin crew helped passengers find their seats.
items.note: The people working inside an aircraft who care for passengers; crew can take a singular or plural verb.

items.pt: desembarcar do avião; sair do avião
items.example: Please wait until the aircraft stops before you get off the plane.
items.note: Get off is used for leaving a plane, bus or train.

items.example: Follow the signs through the terminal building.
items.note: The airport building used by passengers.

items.pt: retirada de bagagens; esteira de bagagens
items.example: We collected our suitcases at baggage reclaim.
items.note: The area where arriving travellers collect their checked luggage.

items.example: You can collect your luggage after passport control.
items.note: Collect means pick up something waiting for you.

items.example: Officials at customs may inspect your bags.
items.note: The government department that checks goods brought into a country.

items.example: We went through customs without any problems.
items.note: Go through means pass the required official checks.

items.example: I followed the green sign marked Nothing to Declare.
items.note: A customs expression used when you are not declaring any restricted or taxable goods.

items.pt: voo de volta; voo de retorno
items.example: Our return flight leaves on Sunday evening.
items.note: A flight taking you back towards where your journey began.

sectionsChecked: A: Departure; airport check-in scene, boarding information, safety instructions and common mistakes
B: Arrival; cabin crew, terminal, baggage reclaim and customs
Exercises 47.1–47.4; compound terms, question answers, email and personal use

units.title: Unit 48 — Hotels and restaurants
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 48. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Describe common hotel facilities, room types and room equipment.
Book and manage accommodation using available, fully booked, in advance, check in and check out.
Reserve a restaurant table and distinguish starters, main courses and desserts.
Ask about service charges and use leave a tip appropriately.
Order food politely and distinguish rare, medium and well-done steak and still versus sparkling water.

items.example: The hotel facilities include a swimming pool and a restaurant.
items.note: Facilities are services, equipment or places provided for guests.

items.example: The hotel is located near the train station.
items.note: Located describes where a building or place is situated.

items.pt: bem no centro de; no coração de
items.example: We stayed in the heart of the old town.
items.note: The heart of a city is its centre or central area.

items.example: We ordered breakfast through room service.
items.note: Hotel staff bring food or drinks to your room.

items.example: Free internet access is available in every room.
items.note: The ability to connect to and use the Internet.

items.example: The air conditioning kept the room cool.
items.note: A system that cools or controls the temperature of the air.

items.example: The hotel offers free parking for guests.
items.note: A place or service for leaving vehicles.

items.example: I booked a single room for my business trip.
items.note: A hotel room intended for one person.

items.pt: quarto de casal; quarto com cama de casal
items.example: They requested a double room with a large bed.
items.note: A room for two people, normally with one double bed.

items.pt: quarto duplo com duas camas de solteiro
items.example: My colleague and I shared a twin room.
items.note: A room for two people with two separate beds.

items.example: Every room is equipped with a small desk.
items.note: Equipped with is followed by the things or facilities provided.

items.example: We watched the news on satellite TV.
items.note: Television that receives channels via satellite.

items.example: The room has a direct-dial telephone beside the bed.
items.note: A telephone that allows direct calls without using a hotel operator.

items.example: There were cold drinks in the mini-bar.
items.note: A small fridge in a hotel room, often stocked with drinks and snacks.

items.example: Leave your passport in the personal safe.
items.note: A secure box for valuable belongings.

items.example: Our bathroom has a bath and a shower.
items.note: In a hotel description, a bath is usually a bathtub.

items.example: The room has a shower but no bath.
items.note: A piece of bathroom equipment that sprays water for washing.

items.example: You can find a hair dryer in the bathroom.
items.note: An electrical appliance for drying hair.

items.example: There are still rooms available for Friday night.
items.note: Available means ready for use or not already taken.

items.example: The hotel is fully booked this weekend.
items.note: All the rooms have been reserved, so no rooms are available.

items.example: We need to book a room before the conference.
items.note: Book is a verb meaning reserve something for future use.

items.example: Could you reserve a room for two nights?
items.note: Reserve is a synonym of book in this context.

items.example: We booked our accommodation in advance.
items.note: Before a particular time or event; not in advanced.

items.pt: fazer check-in; registrar a entrada no hotel
items.example: We can check in after two o'clock.
items.note: At a hotel, report your arrival and receive your room details; verb: check in.

items.example: Ask at reception if you need an extra towel.
items.note: The desk or area where hotel guests are welcomed and assisted.

items.example: We enjoyed our three-night stay at the hotel.
items.note: Noun: the period of time spent in a place; stay can also be a verb.

items.example: We checked out before breakfast.
items.note: At a hotel, settle the bill and leave at the end of a stay.

items.example: It's safer to book a table on Saturday evening.
items.note: To arrange a table at a restaurant before arriving.

items.example: I'd like to make a reservation for two people.
items.note: In restaurants, a reservation is a prior booking of a table.

items.pt: refeição de três pratos; refeição em três etapas
items.example: The restaurant offers a three-course meal for lunch.
items.note: Usually includes a starter, main course and dessert.

items.example: I ordered vegetable soup as a starter.
items.note: The first small course of a meal; British English starter.

items.example: The main course was grilled fish with vegetables.
items.note: The largest or central course of a meal.

items.example: Would you like ice cream for dessert?
items.note: The sweet course eaten at the end of a meal; pronounced with stress on the second syllable.

items.example: The lunch price includes a soft drink.
items.note: To have something as one of the parts of a larger whole.

items.example: The bill includes ten per cent service.
items.note: In this context, service is the charge for being served by restaurant staff.

items.example: Service is included in the total price.
items.note: The service charge is already part of the amount to pay.

items.example: We decided to leave a tip for the waiter.
items.note: Give extra money to thank staff for their service.

items.example: She left a generous tip after dinner.
items.note: Extra money given to service staff; not normally part of the food price.

items.example: The waiter brought us the bill.
items.note: A man who serves customers in a restaurant.

items.example: The waitress explained today's specials.
items.note: A woman who serves customers in a restaurant; server is a gender-neutral alternative.

items.example: We ordered our meals as soon as we sat down.
items.note: At a restaurant, tell staff what you want to eat or drink.

items.example: Are you ready to order, or do you need more time?
items.note: A common question from restaurant staff.

items.example: I'll have the chicken with rice, please.
items.note: Natural phrase for choosing food; not I take the chicken.

items.example: I'd like to start with the soup, please.
items.note: Polite ordering pattern, usually followed by a starter.

items.example: We shared spicy prawns before the main course.
items.note: Prawns are a kind of seafood; spicy describes strongly seasoned or hot food.

items.example: He ordered fillet steak with potatoes.
items.note: A tender cut of beef commonly served as a main course.

items.example: Would you like French fries with your steak?
items.note: Thin pieces of potato fried in oil; often called chips in British English.

items.example: I ordered a mixed salad with my meal.
items.note: A salad containing lettuce and other vegetables.

items.example: I prefer my steak rare.
items.note: For meat, cooked briefly so the inside remains red.

items.example: She asked for her steak medium.
items.note: For meat, cooked more than rare but less than well-done.

items.example: Dad likes his steak well-done.
items.note: For meat, cooked thoroughly without a red centre.

items.word: How would you like your steak?
items.pt: Como você prefere o ponto da carne?
items.example: How would you like your steak? Medium, please.
items.note: A waiter uses this question to ask how thoroughly steak should be cooked.

items.example: Could we have a bottle of mineral water?
items.note: Water containing natural minerals.

items.example: I'd like still water with my meal.
items.note: Water without bubbles; the opposite of sparkling water.

items.example: Do you have sparkling water?
items.note: Water with bubbles; the opposite of still water.

sectionsChecked: A: Hotel facilities and rooms; illustrated hotel listing and room types
B: Staying in a hotel; availability, advance booking, check-in and check-out
C: Going to a restaurant; reservations, meal courses, service and tips
D: Ordering a meal; dialogue, meal choices, steak preparation and water types
Exercises 48.1–48.5; vocabulary grouping, collocations, sentence completion, paraphrase and personal use
